notes_list.title: Hyperconjugation
notes_list.basic_overview: Delocalization involving a sigma C–H/C–C bond adjacent to a pi system or electron-deficient center; it contributes to alkene and carbocation stabilization.
notes_list.extra_info_content: More adjacent donor bonds can increase hyperconjugative stabilization, but molecular geometry and orbital alignment matter. It helps explain alkene substitution and carbocation trends.
notes_list.examples: Tertiary carbocations generally have more hyperconjugative pathways than secondary and primary carbocations. More substituted alkenes are often thermodynamically more stable.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: No special reagent required; this is an intrinsic electronic effect.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: 1. Locate adjacent donor sigma bond. 2. Align it with empty p orbital or π* orbital. 3. Delocalize electron density. 4. Compare number and quality of contributing interactions.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Stabilization changes relative energies; therefore it can alter equilibrium positions and activation barriers indirectly.
notes_list.selectivity_and_stereochemistry: Useful in carbocation stability, alkene stability and orientation arguments.
notes_list.common_traps: Hyperconjugation is not simply “resonance with no bond”; it involves sigma-to-p/π orbital donation.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
